newsitem.title: USA: Pilot unhurt after Statue of Liberty ditching.
newsitem.headline: Pilot unhurt after Statue of Liberty ditching.

text.p: A pilot was uninjured after ditching his small plane Sunday in the Hudson River near the Statue of Liberty, police said.

The pilot, Abraham Moses, 57, of Forest Hills in the city's borough of Queens, put the plane down shortly before noon after radioing the Teterboro, New Jersey, control tower that he had lost power in his engine, a police spokesman said.
Moses was rescued by an unidentified man in a Jet Ski who dropped him off at Liberty State Park, and he refused medical attention, the spokesman said.

His Piper Cherokee Archer sank in the river. Police harbour patrol units, scuba divers and the Army Corps of Engineers later lifted the plane out of the water and towed it to Morris Canal in Jersey City.

Police said Moses left Teterboro Airport at 9 a.m. EDT and was returning two hours later when his plane ran into trouble. "He put the plane down in the water at Liberty Park between Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty," the spokesman said.
